title: SRE cross-shift handoff + SLO triage briefing - 2026-09-14
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the cross-shift briefing for the week of 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-14. Intended audience: current on-call, next on-call, and product/platform owners who own the SLOs referenced below. Use this as the single source for open action items, incident summaries that need follow-up, and SLO health flags to triage during the upcoming rotation.

TL;DR (two-line):
- Major user-facing incident on 2026-09-10 (INC-3452) caused degraded token throughput for hosted-api in us-west-2 for ~47m; primary cause: cache eviction storm + fallback thundering. Follow-ups required: cache throttling rate limit + longer lockback windows.
- SLOs: embeddings ingestion SLO for dedicated customers slipped from 99.9% -> 99.2% in the 7-day window; we have a mitigation and a rollback plan staged.

Quick status snapshot:
- Current pager queue: 1 P0 (monitoring only, scheduled rollback), 3 P1s (performance regressions), 6 P2s (alerts and runbook items).
- Customer-impacting incidents this week: 1 (INC-3452).
- Upcoming maintenance: redis cluster planned scaling (2026-09-20 02:00-04:00 UTC) — low traffic window; notify CS and product owners.

Incidents (short summaries + owner + follow-ups):
1) INC-3452 — hosted-api token throughput degradation (2026-09-10 02:17 UTC)
   - Symptoms: increased tail latency and 5xx spikes across hosted-api endpoints serving text-generation; sustained queueing on GPU workers; some requests dropped to fallback model variant (lower perf).
   - Duration: detection -> mitigation ~47 minutes; full normalcy after cache-policy rollback ~1h20m from start due to KV warm-up.
   - Root cause (initial): a new prefix-caching policy change (PR #2143) introduced aggressive prefix eviction logic. Under a traffic spike (internal batch job + user traffic), cache misses rose and the fallback path caused many concurrent cold-start loads to hit model servers, saturating max-concurrency semaphores.
   - Owner: Mateo Ruiz (SRE) + Evan Cho (serving-runtime).
   - Action items: 
     * Short-term (done): revert PR #2143 and re-enable previous cache TTLs (Rolled back 02:58 UTC).
     * Short-term (open): add a temporary global in-flight load limiter on fallback model path (SRE-892) — aim to throttle new cold inits to 10/min across region. (Owner: Mateo)
     * Medium-term (open): refine eviction algorithm to consider recent-KV-hit-rate and leverage a soft-eviction queue to avoid thundering (owner: serving-runtime). Ticket: GH PR followup (infra #2174).
     * Customer comms: CS draft for impacted tenants (Priya) — in-progress.

2) P1 — embeddings ingestion lag for dedicated nodes (intermittent, week-long)
   - Symptoms: sporadic 503s for ingestion endpoints; background backlog build-up on dedicated pools.
   - Observed window: elevated errors during peak ingest hours (13:00-16:00 UTC) across several dedicated customers.
   - Hypothesis: autoscaler miscalculation when recent CPU samples include occasional micro-bursts; scaling cooldown too short, thrash + cold start.
   - Owner: Priya Sharma (infra-autoscale) + Eng-Optimize.
   - Action items:
     * Increase autoscaler cooldown for dedicated pools to 5m from 1m (staged change) — test in canary (done in canary, needs prod rollout).
     * Implement percentile-based CPU sample window (10th-90th) for scale-up decisions (follow-up design doc, SRE-901).

SLO health & metrics (7d rolling):
- Hosted API availability (prod): target 99.95%
  * 7d observed: 99.82% -> flagged (primary contributor: INC-3452 spike).
  * Recommendation: escalate to platform product owners; consider 24h retrospective.
- Embeddings ingestion (dedicated): target 99.9%
  * 7d observed: 99.2% -> requires mitigation; customers A & B reported timeouts.
- Latency p95 (text-gen short): target 250ms
  * 7d observed p95: 320ms (partly due to fallback model usage during incident windows).

On-call handoff notes (for next rotation):
- Watchlist for next 24-48h:
  * Monitor fallback model concurrency (metric: serving.fallback.concurrent) — threshold > 80 triggers P1 alert.
  * KV cache miss rate per prefix (metric: cache.prefix.miss_rate) — sustained > 0.12 for 10m is concerning.
  * Redis memory churn on primary cluster (redis.usw2.primary.mem_churn) — correlated with eviction storms.
- Handoff checklist items completed:
  * Primary runbooks checked: edge-caching, fallback-throttle, gpu-saturation (links in linked_artifacts).
  * Credentials and escalation path validated (PagerDuty playbook snapshot attached).
  * Rotation logs for previous shift attached (see incident timelines).
- Knowledge transfers pending:
  * Evan to run a 30-minute walkthrough of the updated eviction metrics for next on-call (scheduled 2026-09-16 16:00 UTC).

Runbook and tooling changes (short note):
- New micro-runbook entry proposed: "fallback-throttle-temporary" — one-page checklist to immediately cap cold-model initializations after cache storms. Draft in GH: infra/docs/runbooks/fallback-throttle.md (reviewers: SRE + serving-runtime).
- Grafana alert tuning: reduce noise on CPU burst alerts by increasing evaluation window to 3m. PR queued (infra-monitoring #55).

Retrospective notes (start -> what we learned):
- Takeaway 1: aggressive cache eviction is a low-latency risk if fallback model cold-starts are not rate-limited. The two systems (caching policy + model-loading throttle) were modified independently and interacted poorly under load.
- Takeaway 2: autoscaler logic needs robust percentile-window sampling to avoid reacting to micro-bursts. Dedicated workloads have different temporal profiles than hosted API; layered scaling policies needed.
- Takeaway 3: Our incident detection pipeline caught the latency spike quickly, but our automated mitigation cadence (rollback vs. transient limiters) should be clearer in runbooks.

Open action items (owner and ETA):
- Mateo: implement global fallback in-flight limiter (SRE-892) — ETA 2026-09-20.
- Evan: design eviction soft-queue + metricization plan — ETA design doc 2026-09-22.
- Priya: autoscaler cooldown rollout to prod + post-rollout monitoring deck — ETA 2026-09-19.
- Aisha (owner): coordinate customer comms draft & release notes for INC-3452 — ETA 2026-09-16.

Notes to self / friction items (informal):
- We keep reusing the same metric names across services; a small normalization effort would help dashboards be less confusing during multi-service incidents.
- Still seeing friction between product owners and SRE on acceptable fallback quality thresholds; schedule a 30m sync to align guardrails.

Meeting schedule & invites (relevant):
- Post-incident blameless retros (30m): 2026-09-17 15:00 UTC (invite to SRE, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, CS).
- Runbook walkthrough: Evan -> on-call + next -> 2026-09-16 16:00 UTC.

Appendix (supporting links & logs):
- Incident timeline snippets: 2026-09-10 02:17 DETECT -> 02:28 Escalation -> 02:36 first mitigation (circuit) -> 02:58 rollback commit -> 03:40 steady state.
- Key logs: link to splunk search (SPL: index=prod "INC-3452") — posted to linked_artifacts.

If you are taking next on-call: read the short checklist above, ping Mateo if you see repeat cache-eviction patterns, and keep the fallback model throttle as the first automated mitigation in your playbook.

-- Aisha
